newsitem.title: PERU: Peru approves two new hydrocarbon contracts.
newsitem.headline: Peru approves two new hydrocarbon contracts.

text.p: Peru's Energy and Mines Ministry has approved two new contracts to private oil companies to explore and develop hydrocarbon fields in the north-eastern jungle region, officials said Friday.
The first contract to explore and develop Block 72, between the departments of Loreto and San Martin, was awarded to the Peruvian subsidiary of Occidental Petroleum Corp.
The second contract to explore and develop Blocks 55A, 55B and 55C in the department of Loreto was jointly awarded to Barrett Resources' and Advantage Resources' local units.
Officials could not give more detail of the price of the contracts or the quantity of reserves at the sites.

Energy and Mines Minister Alberto Pandolfi said this week that the government hoped to sign with private oil companies 14 new contracts by the end of next year for the exploration or development of hydrocarbon fields.
He added that 33 contracts, giving concessions to private companies, were currently in effect - 18 for exploration, and 15 for exploitation.
In addition to the contracts with private oil companies, the government is in the midst of a piecemeal privatization of its oil assets belonging to state-run Petroperu.
